text:
zoe: quick heads-up from onboarding sessions: multiple teams hit confusing hangs using Generator.Stream with context cancel + auth rotation. users expect ctx cancel to be enough but we spawn internal handshake goroutines that can outlive caller ctx in some races.

mike: can you share a short repro or pattern we can test?

zoe: pattern is simple: start stream with background goroutine rotating credentials and calling client.AuthRefresh(), then cancel ctx shortly after start. sometimes dial/handshake goroutines stay blocked. minimal pattern posted to issue #1321.

hana: this matches the Resume() complaint earlier. two pragmatic fixes: (A) add an explicit Close()/Stop() on the stream object so callers can force-terminate transports, or (B) make every handshake derive a per-stream ctx that runtime cancels when the stream is closed/drained.

pablo: ergonomics note: we should avoid breaking callers who like range-style channel iteration. propose adding a StreamObject API with Next()/Close()/Ctx() and keep channel-returning Stream(ctx) as a compatibility shim that wraps the object. deprecate shim later.

emily: docs + sampleapps action: update quickstart to show proper pattern (defer stream.Close()), and add a small example demonstrating how to coordinate a background token rotator: rotate tokens only when no handshakes in-flight or use small retry windows. also add a stress test that asserts goroutine growth doesn't occur.

mike: impl note: transport dialers should select on both handshake ctx and a close channel so blocked net.Dials get unblocked on Close(). also make Close() idempotent and safe to call concurrently.

hana: tests: handshake-cancel-no-leak, close-idempotent-race, and channel-shim-parity. include a fake auth server that returns 401 mid-handshake to exercise retry paths.

zoe: will draft PR with object API + shim + tests and add metric active_stream_handles for support. assigning to @mike for runtime review. will ping sampleapps folks for example edits.

ci-bot: created draft PR zoe/stream-api-close-ownership (WIP) - build queued

pablo: one more DX request: add a short "stream ownership" section in generator README explaining best practices (defer Close, prefer object API, avoid auth rotation during handshake) and a small migration snippet from channel iteration to Next()/Close().

emily: can do once PR lands. also add a snippet for Resume() showing WaitGroup + stream.Ctx() monitoring for background workers.

zoe: thanks all 4 will follow up with PR link when ready.
